config.bootstrap_resamples_note: this value is threaded into aggregate() and appears as n_resamples in every bootstrap entry; the two cannot disagree
config.bootstrap_note: 200000 resamples. A 400-seed sweep at 2000 resamples put the upper bound of the ncm p@5 paraphrase delta strictly below zero for 41.2 percent of seeds and exactly at zero for the rest, because these metrics are discrete and the bootstrap distribution of the mean has atoms. No conclusion here is gated on a strict inequality against such an atom; a bound within CI_ZERO_TOL of zero is reported as sitting on zero.
config.scale_note: the shipped numbers are the committed defaults with no flags: max_conversations=20 and bootstrap=200000. A --smoke run reads 4 conversations and is a validation run only, never the shipped result.
config.weights_note: shipped defaults, unmodified by this script
config.relevance_definition: a stored turn is relevant iff it shares the held-out query turn's corpus session_id
config.oracle_leak: none; the query auto-state is inferred from the query text alone and no query-side input derives from the label
config.state_channel_control: store.auto_state.state assigned directly, because retrieve_top_k_fast ignores its s_current_normalized argument

discovery_phase.also_in: experiments/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md lines 319-320 (Experiment 6 section). Line 319 carries the semantic_emotional pair and line 320 the ncm_cached_full pair. Lines 257-258 do NOT hold these values; that location is a speed claim about retrieve_semantic_only.
discovery_phase.what_the_two_conditions_actually_are: Two retrieval SYSTEMS, not two query conditions. 'semantic_emotional' is the ncm.retrieval.retrieve_semantic_emotional baseline and 'ncm_cached_full' is retrieve_top_k_fast with use_strength=True. Both run on the SAME 144 queries.
discovery_phase.misattribution: exp6 has NO verbatim query arm. Every one of its 144 queries is a paraphrase: exp6_current_memory_systems_vs_ncm.py line 120 comments 'Query prompts are category-level paraphrases, not exact memory strings', the JSON records dataset.query_type = 'category paraphrases (not exact memory strings)', and the txt header reads '144 paraphrase queries'. The audit note appears to have read that dataset descriptor as an experimental condition and reported a system-vs-system ablation as a paraphrase regression. No paraphrase regression was measured anywhere in exp6.
discovery_phase.how_the_averages_are_formed: category_avg and state_avg are the unweighted mean of P@1, P@3, P@5 and P@10. Those four components are NOT in the standing[] record, which holds only system, category_avg, state_avg and latency_ms_avg. They are in the systems[] array of the same JSON file, in the entry with the matching 'system' field, under the dicts 'category_p_at_k' and 'state_p_at_k' keyed '1', '3', '5' and '10'. Verified: systems[] semantic_emotional category_p_at_k (0.9375+0.9167+0.8611+0.7903)/4 = 0.8764 and systems[] ncm_cached_full state_p_at_k (0.625+0.6111+0.5903+0.5076)/4 = 0.5835.
discovery_phase.ruled_out: exp19, exp20 and exp21_multihop_reasoning are NOT the source. None of them computes a category_p_at_k or state_p_at_k metric, none writes a JSON result file, and none has a directory under experiments/results/. Attribution to exp6 is positive rather than by elimination: the exp6 JSON contains all four values as named fields and its per-k components reproduce them arithmetically.
discovery_phase.separate_oracle_leak_found_in_exp6: NEEDS ACTION, reported for the orchestrator and not relied on here. In exp6 the query's state vector is STATE_ARCHETYPES[q['state_name']] (lines 265-266) while state_p_at_k's ground truth is defined as memories whose state tag equals that same q['state_name'] (line 273), and each memory's stored state is that archetype plus uniform noise of +/-0.05 (line 165). The query-side state input is therefore derived from the relevance label, which is an oracle leak by the definition used in this audit. Both the 0.7672 and the 0.5835 state_avg figures consume it, so neither is a deployable-condition number.

dataset.paraphrase_provenance: HAND-AUTHORED by the experimenter; not a corpus field. The relevance label is corpus-derived on both arms.
dataset.random_guess_definition: mean over queries of n_relevant / store_size; independent of k
dataset.strength_note: measured: 0 of 14 evaluated conversations have a non-unit strength cache. no reinforce() is called, so every strength is 1.0 and the strength modulator is exactly 1.0, which makes the four-channel decomposition exact. The run aborts if this count is not zero.

decomposition_gate.note: the run returns 1 and writes nothing when this fails

random_baseline_per_metric.definition: Monte Carlo over uniformly random rankings of each target's own store, scored with the same precision_at_k, ndcg_at_k and reciprocal_rank functions used for the real runs, then averaged over targets.

orthography_confound.method: fixed hand-built list of 41 British/American spelling pairs, whole-word case-folded match; a paraphrase counts if it uses the British form and its source turn does not
orthography_confound.limitation: the wordlist is hand-built and not exhaustive, so this count is a lower bound on orthographic divergence

emo_state_offset.note: pre_states[i] is the state passed to encode_emotional for memory i; post_snapshots[i] is memory i's auto_state_snapshot, written by MemoryStore.add after ingesting memory i's text. A zero in the shift-by-one field confirms the vectors are the same sequence offset by exactly one turn.

state_padding.w_emo_rank_loss_note: W_emo has shape (3, 7), so it maps the 5 informative state dimensions into 3 and cannot be inverted; encode_emotional then L2-normalizes the result, which discards its magnitude. Both are reasons the d_emo / d_state correlation is below 1.
state_padding.note: AutoStateTracker emits 5 dimensions while SentenceEncoder.state_dim defaults to 7, so encode_state and encode_emotional zero-pad and dimensions 6 and 7 carry no information. Note that the composite state channel compares auto_state_snapshot directly at 5 dims, so the padding affects the emotional projection, not d_state.

state_controllability.probe_a_note: True confirms retrieve_top_k_fast ignores s_current_normalized; the argument cannot be used to control the state channel.
state_controllability.probe_b_note: True confirms store.auto_state.state DOES drive the channel, so a null state result under inferred states is a property of the inference and not an uncontrolled input.

query_state_pairwise_l2.scope: POOLED over both query conditions, so it mixes across-target variation with the within-target verbatim-vs-paraphrase shift that verbatim_vs_paraphrase_state_l2 reports separately

state_dispersion.analytic_note: alpha*|signal-0.5| with signal bounded in [0,1] and alpha = [0.15,0.15,0.15,0.20,0.25]; the largest move one utterance can make in each dimension starting from the neutral 0.5 state.

aggregate.clustering_note: the 48 paired targets come from 14 conversations, so the observations are clustered; every regression entry carries both a target-level and a conversation-level bootstrap CI plus a measured ICC(1) and effective n

wilcoxon_on_char_delta.method_note: scipy.stats.wilcoxon with method set explicitly; 'auto' would have used the normal approximation whenever zeros or ties occur

query_length_match.note: Two separate questions. wilcoxon_on_char_delta asks whether the arms differ in length at all. paired_length_vs_metric_spearman asks whether a metric's per-target movement tracks that target's own length change: x is the paired per-target character-count change from verbatim to hand-authored paraphrase, y is the paired per-target change in the named metric. A null rho does not clear an arm-level length difference; the two are different quantities.

conclusion: Scale: 48 paired targets from 14 conversations, 200000 bootstrap resamples, hand-authored paraphrases.

NCM P@5 changes by -0.0083 from verbatim to hand-authored paraphrase queries. Target-level 95pct CI [-0.0542, +0.0375]; conversation-level cluster CI [-0.0553, +0.0356], which is the one to read because the targets are clustered. The cluster CI includes zero, so no paraphrase regression is established at this sample size. 24 of 48 targets changed on this metric; the smallest difference this design would detect at 80 percent power is 0.0645.

The semantic-only baseline P@5 changes by -0.0083 from verbatim to hand-authored paraphrase queries. Target-level 95pct CI [-0.0500, +0.0333]; conversation-level cluster CI [-0.0520, +0.0298], which is the one to read because the targets are clustered. The cluster CI includes zero, so no paraphrase regression is established at this sample size. 24 of 48 targets changed on this metric; the smallest difference this design would detect at 80 percent power is 0.0577.

The targets are clustered by conversation, not independent. Measured ICC(1) for the NCM P@5 delta is +0.0069 over 14 conversations of mean size 3.43, a design effect of 1.017 and an effective sample size of 47.21 against 48 nominal observations.

No difference in paraphrase P@5 loss between the composite and the bare encoder was detected: +0.0000, conversation-level cluster CI [-0.0213, +0.0255], zero strictly interior. At n=48 the smallest difference this design would detect at 80 percent power is 0.0289 P@5, so a composite-added fragility below that remains possible. 6 of 48 targets changed on this measure.

MRR RISES under hand-authored paraphrase, by +0.0194 for NCM and +0.0002 for the semantic-only baseline. That is larger in magnitude than the largest P@5 movement (0.0083) and opposite in sign to it, so the word regression does not describe every metric in this table. The NCM MRR conversation-level cluster CI is [-0.0474, +0.0847], which includes zero, so the direction is not established.

The two arms are NOT length-matched at this scale. The hand-authored paraphrases are longer by +5.6 characters on average (+5.6 percent), exact Wilcoxon on the paired character counts p = 0.0005. Query length is therefore a second manipulated variable alongside rewording, and this design cannot separate the two.

No paired length-versus-metric Spearman correlation reaches p < 0.05 over the 6 metrics tested, the largest being semantic_only__mrr rho -0.0998 p 0.4996. No metric's per-target movement was found to track per-target length change. This does NOT clear the arm-level length difference reported above: a per-target rank correlation and a difference in arm means are different quantities, and with 48 targets this test is underpowered against a small one.

Under verbatim queries, d_sem supplies 91.7 percent of the SUMMED per-channel across-candidate standard deviation; the shares are sem 91.7, emo 1.0, state 5.4, time 1.9 percent. This is a share of a sum of standard deviations, not a variance decomposition, because std(sum) does not equal sum(std) unless the channels are perfectly correlated. A variance-based share would put d_sem higher, so this figure understates its dominance.

Under paraphrase queries, d_sem supplies 91.8 percent of the SUMMED per-channel across-candidate standard deviation; the shares are sem 91.8, emo 1.0, state 5.3, time 1.9 percent. This is a share of a sum of standard deviations, not a variance decomposition, because std(sum) does not equal sum(std) unless the channels are perfectly correlated. A variance-based share would put d_sem higher, so this figure understates its dominance.

gamma*d_state has 18.3 times less across-candidate dispersion than alpha*d_sem (0.003240 against 0.059254), so despite carrying weight gamma=0.3 it rarely changes the order. It is not incapable of reordering: no single-channel ablation was run here, so the extra channels' contribution to the ranking is not attributed.
retrieve_top_k_fast ignored its s_current_normalized argument: two opposite argument values produced an identical ranking.
Assigning store.auto_state.state DID change the distances, so the state channel was genuinely driven and the low dispersion above is not a false negative from an uncontrolled input.

Across targets within the verbatim arm alone, pairwise L2 between the 48 inferred query states spans 0.0052 to 0.0792 over 1128 pairs, against a per-dimension single-step ceiling of at most 0.125, because AutoStateTracker.update applies one EMA step from the neutral 0.5 vector.

Across targets within the paraphrase arm alone, pairwise L2 between the 48 inferred query states spans 0.0032 to 0.0779 over 1128 pairs, against a per-dimension single-step ceiling of at most 0.125, because AutoStateTracker.update applies one EMA step from the neutral 0.5 vector.
Within a target, the verbatim-to-paraphrase state shift is a separate and smaller quantity: mean L2 0.0128 over 48 targets. The earlier pooled figure mixed these two scopes.

d_emo and d_state correlate at Pearson r = 0.2939 across candidates under verbatim queries. They are built from RELATED BUT DIFFERENT vectors, not the same one: e_emotional is a fixed linear projection W_emo of the PRE-update auto-state, while d_state compares the POST-update auto_state_snapshot of the same memory. Measured over 567 stored memories in 14 stores, 0 pairs are identical and the mean L2 gap is 0.017796, while the max L2 between the pre-update state at index i and the snapshot at index i-1 is 0.000e+00, which places them exactly one turn apart. r stays below 1 for two further reasons: W_emo has shape (3, 7), so it maps the 5 informative state dimensions into 3 and loses rank, and encode_emotional L2-normalizes the projection, which discards its magnitude (measured output norm 1.0000).
